title: Savings Cartography: field lab roadmap for batching, caching, and micro-quantization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Run a tightly scoped field lab (Savings Cartography) to map cost savings surface area across three levers: request-level batching, KV/prefix caching, and targeted micro-quantization profiles. This ticket owns the product roadmap, success metrics, experiment plan, and rollout decision criteria for the first tranche of customers used in the field lab.

High-level deliverables:
1) Playbook: experiment runbook for each lever (triggering criteria, guardrails, rollback).
2) Signal spec: consolidated dashboard (token cost, p50/p95 latency, error rate, quality delta on eval prompts) and alert thresholds.
3) Cohort plan: list of 6 pilot customers grouped by workload archetype (low-latency chat, high-throughput batch embedding, mixed).
4) Release toggle/rollout plan with canary windows, fallback models, and SLA exemptions.
5) Eval set & automated quality checks with baseline vs. variant scoring.

Success metrics (primary): net token-dollar savings >= 12% across pilot cohort at stable QoQ quality (mean BLEU/ROUGE/bert-sim change <= 0.6% absolute), p95 latency within 15% of baseline for latency-sensitive cohorts. Secondary: adoption signal >= 3 teams request enabling after pilot.

Plan & timeline: discovery & artifact alignment (2 weeks), infra & signals build (3 weeks), pilot execution (4 weeks), analysis & roll decision (1 week). Total: 10 weeks.

Risks & mitigations: Quality regressions from quantization (mitigate with candidate scoring & auto-rollback), increased p95 from aggressive batching (mitigate with dynamic batch caps and latency SLO routing), telemetry gaps (mitigate with instrumentation spike before pilot).

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Eng leads (Martin O'Connor, S. Liu), Research (Dr. Carla Ruiz), DevRel for customer coordination (T. Nguyen), CX for SLAs (R. Martinez).

Artifacts: Confluence playbook https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/SAVINGS-CARTOGRAPHY, experiment design doc Drive https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CartoLab, monitoring dashboard https://prometheus.redwood.company/d/fieldlab/savings-cartography, baseline infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4392.

Acceptance criteria: playbook published, dashboard populated with synthetic & historical signals, 6 pilot customers consented, infra toggles tested end-to-end, run of at least 2 full-week experiments with automated quality checks passing for at least one variant per lever.
comments: 2025-02-19: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. Agreed to limit initial quantization profiles to 4-bit mixed with activation-aware calibration. Action: ENG to prototype quant matrix by 02-27. (Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-repo/issues/87)

2025-02-24: Research flagged potential hallucination regressions for conversational prompts at extreme quant levels. Decided to include a paired human-eval pass for first two customers. Assigned to Carla. Estimated 3 evaluators for 2 weeks.

2025-02-28: Observability spike complete. Dashboard now shows token cost per request + by-model breakdown. Missing: latency heatmap by customer. ENG-5590 added to dependencies to implement heatmap. Priority for next sprint.

2025-03-02: Design review with DevRel: cohort consent flow and UI copy approved. PR for consent modal: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2210. UX asked for clearer rollback CTA in early windows.

2025-03-04: Decision log: Start field lab with conservative batching policy (max 8 concurrent requests, dynamic TTL for KV cache = 30s) and two quant profiles (q4_a = aggressive, q6_c = conservative). If quality delta > 1% then auto-revert. Logged in playbook.

2025-03-05: PM sync: One pilot customer (acme-ml) onboarded; they are mixed workload and requested exclusion of low-latency chat endpoints. Workaround: route chat to dedicated low-latency pool. Next: confirm three more pilots by 2025-03-12.
2025-03-05: Action items: ENG to add per-route rollout tags in telemetry (ENG-4212), Research to finalize eval set (DR-092), Ops to prepare rollback runbook and incident contacts.
